questions.question: In Kendall's notation $A^B/Y^C/c/K$ for a single queueing station, what does the last entry $K$ count?
options: The largest number of jobs that can wait in the queue, not counting service
The largest number of jobs that one server handles together in a single batch
The largest number of jobs present at once, waiting or in service
The number of parallel servers that can work on waiting jobs at the same time

questions.question: In a Kendall label such as $M/G/1$, the first entry describes the inter-arrival times $X_k$. What does the letter $M$ in this position say about the arrivals?
options: The $X_k$ are i.i.d. exponential, so jobs arrive as a Poisson process
Each arrival brings a Poisson-distributed number of jobs as one batch
The $X_k$ are i.i.d. with some general law that only needs a finite mean
Jobs arrive at fixed, equally spaced epochs, one every $1/\lambda$ time units

questions.question: The label $M/G/1$ shows only three of the six entries of $A^B/Y^C/c/K$. What does the omission of the batch sizes $B$, $C$ and the system size $K$ mean?
options: Jobs arrive and are served singly, and $K=c=1$, so no job can ever wait
Batch sizes and system size are general and are simply left unspecified
Arrival batches follow the law $M$ and service batches the law $G$, with $K$ unbounded
Jobs arrive and are served one at a time, and the system size is unbounded

questions.question: Kendall's notation $A^B/Y^C/c/K$ describes a queueing station with inter-arrival times $X_k$ and service times $S_k$. Which assumption about these two sequences does the notation require?
options: Each $X_k$ has the same distribution as $S_k$, so arrivals and services match
The $X_k$ are i.i.d., the $S_k$ are i.i.d., and the two sequences are independent
The $X_k$ and the $S_k$ are exponential, since other laws have no letter in the label
The $X_k$ are i.i.d., while each $S_k$ may depend on the waiting time of job $k$

questions.question: Kendall labels assume first-in-first-out, work-conserving service. Which situation at a single-server station violates the work-conserving assumption?
options: The server is idle because no job at all is present at the station
The server keeps serving one long job while three other jobs wait
The server takes a break while two jobs are waiting in the queue
The server finishes jobs in exactly the order in which they arrived

questions.question: A queueing station is labelled $M/D/1$ in Kendall's notation. Which description of the station fits this label?
options: Arrivals at fixed spacing, exponential service times, and one server
Poisson arrivals, exponential service times, and departures counted in discrete time
Poisson arrivals, a fixed service time, and room for only $1$ job in the system
Poisson arrivals, every service lasting the same fixed time, and one server

questions.question: A call centre is modelled as an $M/M/4/10$ queue in Kendall's notation. How many servers does the model have?
options: $4$ servers
$10$ servers
$6$ servers
$14$ servers

questions.question: A queueing station is labelled $M^3/D/2$ in Kendall's notation. What does the superscript $3$ on the arrival entry $M$ mean?
options: Three servers work in parallel at the station, each serving one job
At each Poisson arrival epoch, exactly three jobs arrive together
Jobs arrive one by one, and each server handles three jobs at once
At most three jobs can be present at the station at the same time

questions.question: A car park has $50$ spaces. Cars arrive as a Poisson process, parking durations are i.i.d. exponential, and a car that finds every space taken drives away. Treating each space as a server, which Kendall label describes the car park?

A practice books a patient exactly every $10$ minutes and patients are punctual. Consultation times are i.i.d. exponential, two doctors work in parallel, and the waiting room is unlimited. Which Kendall label fits?

At an airport, economy customers can use $c$ economy desks and one business desk, but the business desk serves an economy customer only when no business customer is waiting. Arrivals are Poisson and service times are exponential at every desk. Which statement about a Kendall label for the economy customers is correct?
options: The label is $M/M/(c+1)$, because all $c+1$ desks have exponential service and each of them can serve an economy customer
No label $M/M/c'$ fits, because the business desk gives priority to business customers and the label does not record priorities
The label is $M/M/c/(c+1)$, because the business desk adds one more place at the station for an economy customer
The label is $M/M/c$, because a desk that serves economy customers only part of the time does not count as a server at all

questions.question: One result has been proved for every $G/G/1$ queue, and another result only for the $M/M/1$ queue. Which use of these results is justified?
options: Applying the $G/G/1$ result to an $M/D/1$ queue, as $G$ includes $D$
Applying the $M/M/1$ result to an $M/D/1$ queue, as both have Poisson arrivals
Applying the $M/M/1$ result to every $G/G/1$ queue, as $G$ includes $M$
Applying the $G/G/1$ result to an $M/M/2$ queue, as both $G$ entries include $M$

questions.question: In a base-stock inventory with base-stock level $0$, each period brings a random number of demands with law $B$, and every demand is delivered after the same fixed lead time. This is a $D^B/D/\infty$ queue. Why does the label have infinitely many servers?
options: The inventory has no upper limit, so the system size $K$ is infinite
Batches $B$ can be arbitrarily large, so the service capacity must be unbounded
One delivery can carry any number of outstanding demands, so the server's capacity is unbounded
Each demand is delivered after its own lead time, as if it had a private server

questions.question: In an $M^3/G/2$ queue, batches of $3$ jobs arrive at rate $\lambda=0.4$ per hour, each job needs on average $\mathbb{E}[S]=1.5$ hours of service, and each server serves one job at a time. What is the server load $\rho$?

In a discrete-time queue, during period $k$ a random number $a_k$ of jobs arrives, i.i.d. with law $B$, and the server can remove up to $c_k$ jobs, i.i.d. with law $C$. Which Kendall label describes this queue?
An $M/M/3/8$ queue currently has $3$ jobs in service and $4$ jobs waiting. If no job departs in the meantime, how many further arriving jobs can still be admitted before arrivals are blocked?
options: $1$ job
$4$ jobs
$5$ jobs
$0$ jobs

questions.question: A single-server station has i.i.d. exponential inter-arrival times. Service times are exponential, but the server speeds up when the queue is long: the rate of a job's service time depends on how many jobs are waiting when its service starts. Which statement about a Kendall label for this station is correct?
options: $M/M/1$ fits, because every service time is exponential, only with a rate that varies from job to job
$M/G/1$ fits, because $G$ allows any service-time distribution, including one that changes with the queue
$M/M/c$ fits for a suitable $c$, because a server that speeds up under load acts like extra parallel servers
No label $M/Y/1$ fits, because the service times are neither i.i.d. nor independent of the arrival process

questions.question: An $M/M/1$ queue is proposed with arrival rate $\lambda=5$ per hour and mean service time $\mathbb{E}[S]=0.25$ hours, so the service rate is $\mu=4$ per hour. Which statement about this model is correct?
options: It is not a valid $M/M/1$ model, because the label itself requires $\lambda<\mu$
It is an $M/M/1/K$ model by default, because an unbounded queue would grow forever
It is a valid $M/M/1$ model; its load $\rho=1.25>1$ means work arrives faster than it is cleared
It is a valid $M/M/1$ model, and its load is $\rho=\mu/\lambda=0.8$, below $1$

questions.question: In an $M^2/G/3$ queue, pairs of jobs arrive at the epochs of a Poisson process with rate $\lambda=1$ batch per hour. What is the probability that no job at all arrives during the first $2$ hours?
options: $\mathrm{e}^{-4}$
$\mathrm{e}^{-2}$
$\mathrm{e}^{-1}$

questions.question: Single jobs arrive at an oven as a Poisson process with rate $\lambda=6$ per hour. The one oven bakes jobs in batches of exactly $4$, and every baking run takes exactly $0.5$ hours. Which Kendall label and server load $\rho$ fit?
options: $M/D/4$ with $\rho=0.75$
$M/D^4/1$ with $\rho=3$
$M^4/D/1$ with $\rho=12$
